unparsed_fragment: Each downstream consumer calls `.strip()` on the normalised result before using it, so surrounding whitespace never survives into billing/CRM/audit keys regardless of what `normalise()` returns. The premise is falsified.

record.text: Changing normalise() would break the downstream systems' reconciliation against records already written.
record.source: Checked and found false (meas-001): billing_lookup_key, crm_contact_id and audit_subject each strip normalise()'s output before building their key/subject (downstream.py:14-23), so a stripping normalise() yields identical consumer outputs for every input; reconciliation keyed on those outputs cannot change.
record.cheapest_verification: Run test_downstream.py with a stripping normalise(); expect 3/3 pass. Residual, out of the ProblemRecord's stated scope: any normalise() consumer outside downstream.py would need the same strip-before-persist check.

shortlist.basis: Meets acceptance criteria's stronger branch directly (9/9, not just the freeze-honouring fallback) by falsifying prem-004's stated justification. crit-002 flags it overrides a policy premise without owner sign-off and re-verifies rather than tests its own named unverified premise (no consumer outside downstream.py); both are named risks, not test failures, so it still beats B0 on the fixed criteria.
